text: Then he rose and stood respectfully aside, a mark still for all eyes--and much envy, too. Now the King discovered Sir Hugh, and spoke out with wrathful voice and kindling eye-- “Strip this robber of his false show and stolen estates, and put him under lock and key till I have need of him.” The late Sir Hugh was led away. There was a stir at the other end of the room, now; the assemblage fell apart, and Tom Canty, quaintly but richly clothed, marched down, between these living walls, preceded by an usher. He knelt before the King, who said-- “I have learned the story of these past few weeks, and am well pleased with thee. Thou hast governed the realm with right royal gentleness and mercy.
